house_a_resident.text: Ey up, come in. Mind your head on the beam, it has had better men than you.
In York, a narrow alley is a snickelway. A man named Mark W. Jones invented the word in 1983 for his book of walks.
Round here a ginnel or a snicket is the same thing, and there are dozens of them. I use them all to dodge the crowds.
If a peregrin is on the Minster tower, stop and watch. They love a tall tower, and they are the fastest bird in the world.

then.text: Back for the Yorkshire Pudding? Kitchen's yours.

else.text: Never open the oven door. Never. I'll know.
Fat smoking hot, batter straight in. Traditionally you eat it first, with gravy, so you fill up before the meat. Thrifty, Yorkshire.
Pop in whenever you've got the makings. Use my kitchen.
